I do that with my Xbox One - external drive support is actually one of the reasons I bought an XB1 instead of a PS4. Being able to do that with Steam is an excellent feature, but PC games tend to be larger in size. Payday 2 for example is ~10GB on the Xbox One and ~27 GB on PC.

One thing I like about the Xbox One over the Xbox 360 is that back in the 360 days, you could install a game from a disc to your hard drive but it was technically different data than the digital version, so you couldn't copy the data to your buddy's 360 and have them buy it in the store - they'd have to order the disc like you did. But with the Xbox One, game data is the same whether it came from a disc or purchased from the digital store, so my buddies and I can install a game from one disc, and then copy the game data to everyone else's Xbox and buy them from the digital store to play immediately.

I guess Steam already kind of is taking that a step forward with the LAN streaming; it's a neat idea to have to only maintain one copy of a game and get to play it on PC or on a living room "console" setup via Steam.
